open_points.subject: Linux host requirement and start proof
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, of any version that runs the sandbox runtime, which the start proves (A03; owner, 2026-10-18).
open_points.question: Which module owns the Linux-host requirement and the decision that startup has proved it, given that State 3 says A20 rule 3 is outside the running kernel and has no module owner, while `sandbox` owns the A03 startup probe?
options: Treat the release/build as the sole owner and let runtime modules rely on the platform guarantee
Make `sandbox` own the runtime host proof as part of `probe_sandbox`
Make `data_provider` own the supported-host policy and let `sandbox` enforce it
open_points.default_guess: Make `sandbox` own the runtime proof while the release/build owns the supported-host declaration.

open_points.subject: Startup order for Linux-specific file opening
open_points.text: `surface.serve_kernel` runs the start in this order: `installation.load_installation`; `bindings.check_installed_instances`; `store.open_store`; `sandbox.probe_sandbox`
open_points.question: How can startup prove the Linux-host condition through A03 only after `installation` and `store` have already performed mandatory Linux-specific `O_NOFOLLOW` opens, with no availability check or non-Linux mode permitted?
options: Move the Linux/sandbox probe before every configuration and store open
Treat the first unconditional `O_NOFOLLOW` use as the host proof and keep the sandbox probe later
Declare host compatibility a pre-start release/launcher precondition rather than something `surface.serve_kernel` proves
open_points.default_guess: Treat Linux compatibility as a release/launcher precondition and keep `sandbox.probe_sandbox` as proof only that the sandbox runtime works.
